plain: The Orion correlation theory holds that the great pyramids at Giza are laid out to match the stars of Orion's belt. The writer Graham Hancock tells Michels the idea came from Robert Bauval, who put it forward in his book The Orion Mystery in 1994. Hancock presents it as a known theory from that book rather than his own. On a later episode, a pyramid researcher named Geoffrey Drumm brings it up himself, saying 'some of these structures are connected to Orion's belt. I think that's true.' Drumm endorses the idea outright but does not credit Bauval or give a date. If true, it would mean the builders planned the site around the sky with a deliberate astronomical design in mind.
